archetypes.scenario: Contractor Quote Audit ($15k+ HVAC / Solar / Remodel)
structure: 1. Peer Empathy Hook ('Got blindsided by the exact same quote last year...')
2. Wholesale vs Retail Cost Breakdown (Equipment, Labor Hours, Margin)
3. Hidden Financed Fee Alert ('Check dealer fee if financing at 0-2.9% — usually adds 25-35% to principal')
4. Three Specific Questions to Ask the Estimator
archetypes.gold_example:
Been through this exact ringer last fall when our 14-year-old gas unit gave up right before winter. A $16,500 quote for a standard 3-ton system is carrying roughly a 60% gross margin.

Here is what is actually in that box:
- Equipment wholesale (3-ton 15.2 SEER2 condenser + air handler): ~$4,400 to $5,200 depending on brand tier.
- Sheet metal transition, pad, line set, disconnect: ~$600.
- Labor: 2 techs, 1 full day (16 total man-hours). Even at $150/hr billable rate, that is $2,400.
- Permitting & disposal: ~$400.
- Fair total cost with healthy 25% contractor profit: ~$10,500–$11,800.

Two things to check before you sign:
1. Are they quoting low-interest financing? Contractors often roll an 18-28% 'dealer fee' directly into the cash price to offer '0% for 60 months'. Ask for the unfinanced cash price.
2. Ask for the Manual J calculation. If they just matched the old 3-ton size without measuring duct CFM and insulation, you risk short-cycling.

If you want to run your regional climate zone numbers against the local utility rebate database, I used this open calculation tool: https://gworky.com/tools/heat-pump-roi-calculator

archetypes.gold_example: The missing variable in the 50 bps refinance math: closing costs. On a $420k balance, 1.5% in fees ($6,300) takes 46 months to break even on a 50 bps spread. If the average homeowner moves or refinances every 4.2 years, the lender captures 92% of your lifetime savings.

gold_example.node_1: Most home buyers treat mortgage points as an automatic win if they plan to stay 'long term'. In reality, points are one of the highest-margin upsells in retail lending — and 68% of borrowers never reach the break-even point.
gold_example.node_2: Paying 1 point ($4,000 on a $400k loan) typically buys down the rate by 0.25%. That saves $66/month. Break-even: 61 months (over 5 years). But if mortgage rates drop 75 bps within 36 months, you refinance anyway — forfeiting $1,624 of unrecouped cash upfront.
gold_example.node_3: Lenders push discount points aggressively near rate cycle pivots because points are earned upfront on day one as non-refundable revenue, insulating their margin against prepayment velocity.
gold_example.node_4: If you have $4,000 in dry powder at closing, deploying it into additional principal on month 1 saves $11,800 in compound interest without locking your capital into a 5-year break-even horizon. What is your hurdle rate for points?
gold_example.node_5: We built a zero-ad, open scenario calculator comparing discount points vs extra principal vs HYSA yield across 30 years: https://gworky.com/tools/mortgage-points-calculator
